entries.content_plain: 2. thy mother-- the mother of Jehoiachin, the representative of David's line in exile with Ezekiel. The "mother" is Judea: "a lioness," as being fierce in catching prey ( Eze 19:3 ), referring to her heathenish practices. Jerusalem was called Ariel (the lion of God) in a good sense ( Is 29:1 ); and Judah "a lion's whelp ... a lion ... an old lion" ( Ge 49:9 ), to which, as also to Nu 23:24 ; 24:9 , this passage alludes. nourished ... among young lions-- She herself had "lain" among lions, that is, had intercourse with the corruptions of the surrounding heathen and had brought up the royal young ones similarly: utterly degenerate from the stock of Abraham. Lay down-- or "couched," is appropriate to the lion, the Arab name of which means "the coucher."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11320"/><div sID="gen20472" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11320"/><hi type="bold">7. knew ... desolate palaces--</hi>that is, claimed as his own their palaces, which he then proceeded to "desolate." The Hebrew, literally "widows"; hence widowed palaces (<reference osisRef="Isa.13.22">Is 13:22</reference>). Vatablus (whom Fairbairn follows) explains it, "He knew (carnally) the widows of those whom he devoured" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.19.6">Eze 19:6</reference>). But thus the metaphor and the literal reality would be blended: the lion being represented as knowing widows. The reality, however, often elsewhere thus breaks through the veil.<div eID="gen20472" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20473" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fulness thereof--</hi>all that it contained; its inhabitants. <div eID="gen20473" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11323"/><div sID="gen20478" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11323"/>10. A new metaphor taken from the vine, the chief of the fruit-bearing trees, as the lion is of the beasts of prey (see <reference osisRef="Ezek.17.6">Eze 17:6</reference>).<div eID="gen20478" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20479" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in thy blood--</hi>"planted when thou wast in thy blood," that is, in thy very infancy; as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.6">Eze 16:6</reference>, when thou hadst just come from the womb, and hadst not yet the blood washed from thee. The Jews from the first were planted in Canaan to take root there [Calvin]. Grotius translates as the Margin, "in thy quietness," that is, in the period when Judah had not yet fallen into her present troubles. English Version is better. Glassius explains it well, retaining the metaphor, which Calvin's explanation breaks, "in the blood of thy grapes," that is, in her full strength, as the red wine is the strength of the grape. <reference osisRef="Gen.49.11">Ge 49:11</reference> is evidently alluded to.<div eID="gen20479" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20480" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">many waters--</hi>the well-watered land of Canaan (<reference osisRef="Deut.8.7-Deut.8.9">De 8:7-9</reference>). <div eID="gen20480" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11324"/><div sID="gen20481" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11324"/><hi type="bold">11. strong rods--</hi>princes of the royal house of David. The vine shot forth her branches like so many scepters, not creeping lowly on the ground like many vines, but trained aloft on a tree or wall. The mention of their former royal dignity, contrasting sadly with her present sunken state, would remind the Jews of their sins whereby they had incurred such judgments.<div eID="gen20481" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20482" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stature--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Dan.4.11">Da 4:11</reference>).<div eID="gen20482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20483" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">among the thick branches--</hi>that is, the central stock or trunk of the tree shot up highest "among its own branches" or offshoots, surrounding it. Emblematic of the numbers and resources of the people. Hengstenberg translates, "among the clouds." But <reference osisRef="Ezek.31.3">Eze 31:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.10.14">10, 14</reference>, supports English Version. <div eID="gen20483" type="x-p"/>
